name: Charles Parker
bio: A gentleman's valet, out of employment at the beginning of 1893 when Taylor picked him and his brother up at the St James's Restaurant bar; aged 21 by his own sworn statement at the April 1895 trial. The first and most damaging Crown witness: his testimony describes sodomy at the Savoy and continued relations at Chapel Street, Park Walk, Tite Street and St James's Place, alongside his admitted £30 share of a Wood-Allen blackmail. Arrested and discharged in the Fitzroy Street raid of August 1894, he enlisted on 3 September 1894 and was traced to his regiment by Queensberry's solicitor at the end of March 1895. Wilde was convicted on all four Parker counts; from prison Wilde wrote of 'my connection with Charley Parker of which you may read a full account in my trial.'
bio_sources: Charles Parker's testimony, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 191-198 (pp. 191, 193, 197 read as IIIF page images 2026-08-03; rest djvu OCR)
Wilde to Robert Ross [1896], Complete Letters (2000), p. 670, with the editors' note 'One of the young men who gave evidence at Wilde's trials' (p. 670 n 1; read at rendered PDF p. 721, 2026-08-03)
bio_note: No birth/death dates found in sources read so far — 'aged 21 at the 1895 trials' per his own testimony. His father was 'a horse dealer' (cross-examination, p. 196). At Taylor's trial he testified again; Grain's cross there opens 'I was previously guilty of this' (djvu OCR, p. 275 region — flagged for verification in the source next session). DATES: NOT FOUND; RECORDED AS UNRECOVERED FROM THE SOURCES CONSULTED (2026-08-03). The age is now verified in the source rather than from OCR: Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde (Notable British Trials), printed p. 191, opening the prosecution evidence at the first criminal trial - 'CHARLES PARKER, examined by Mr. C. F. GILL - I am 21 years of age. I have a brother, William. I have been engaged as a valet and my brother as a groom.' Read as a page image in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, IA PDF p. 230) and the printed folio 191 confirmed. That is an age sworn in April 1895 and nothing more: no birth year is computed from it into the born field. No source consulted gives a date. SWEEP FOR DATES, 2026-08-03 (what was searched): the Complete Letters (2000) OCR mirror plus the General Index; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008), repo PDF; Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDF; Frankel, The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF; Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde, in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, OCR text downloaded and searched, key pages then read as page images); and the open web. The obvious next step is not another book: it is the GRO birth index and the 1881/1891 censuses for a Charles Parker, valet, and his brother William, groom - genealogical work outside what so far could do.
